message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.1","text":"I, Clement, a citizen of Rome, have managed to live the first part of my life with self-control, while from childhood my reflection kept turning the desire within me toward states of dejection and pain. For a thought about death stayed with me—I do not know where it began—repeatedly reminding me that, once dead, I would not exist and no one would ever make mention of me, since boundless time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion: I will be nonexistent, not knowing those who exist, not knowing, not being known, not having come into being, and not coming into being. And did the world ever come into being, and what, then, existed before it came into being? For if it always existed, it also will exist; but if it came into being, it will also be dissolved. And after its dissolution, what in turn will exist, unless perhaps silence and oblivion? And perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"σωφρόνως ζῆσαι","chosen":"to live ... with self-control","rationale":"σωφρόνως can denote chastity more narrowly, but here broadly describes a restrained early life."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐννοίας μου ἐκ παιδὸς ἀπασχολούσης τὴν ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐπιθυμίαν εἴς τε ἀθυμίας καὶ πόνους","chosen":"while from childhood my reflection kept turning the desire within me toward states of dejection and pain","rationale":"The genitive absolute describes his reflection as occupying or diverting his inward desire toward distress."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἀπείρου χρόνου πάντων τὰ πάντα εἰς λήθην φέροντος","chosen":"since boundless time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion","rationale":"Preserves both the universal πάντων and the comprehensive τὰ πάντα."},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ὄντας εἰδώς","chosen":"not knowing those who exist","rationale":"The negative is taken as governing the whole participial phrase, with ὄντας as the object of εἰδώς. Immediate attachment to ὄντας would instead yield the paradoxical alternative “knowing those who do not exist.”"},{"source_quote":"σιγὴ καὶ λήθη","chosen":"silence and oblivion","rationale":"λήθη here denotes the state of being forgotten rather than merely a personal lapse of memory."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἔσομαι δὲ οὐκ ὤν, οὐκ ὄντας εἰδώς","issue":"The verified wording is syntactically defensible but permits two scopes for οὐκ in the second phrase: “not knowing those who exist” or “knowing those who do not exist.” The contextual rendering is given in the text without emending the Greek.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"1.2","text":"Continually pondering these and similar things—I do not know from where—I bore a painful grief so intense that I grew pale and wasted away. Most terrible of all, if ever I resolved to push the concern away as useless, my distress became all the more acute. I was troubled by this, not knowing that I had a noble thought as my housemate, one that would become for me a cause of good immortality, as I later learned by experience and gave thanks to God, the master of all. For the thought that oppressed me at first compelled me to enter upon the investigation and discovery of realities; and then I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of calling blessed.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὀδυνηρὰν εἶχον λύπην τοσοῦτον ὡς ὠχριακότα με τήκεσθαι","chosen":"I bore a painful grief so intense that I grew pale and wasted away","rationale":"Expresses the result construction while retaining both pallor and physical wasting."},{"source_quote":"σύνοικον καλὴν ἔχων ἔννοιαν","chosen":"I had a noble thought as my housemate","rationale":"Preserves the domestic image of σύνοικον rather than reducing it to a thought merely being present."},{"source_quote":"ἀθανασίας ἀγαθῆς αἰτίαν μοι γενησομένην","chosen":"one that would become for me a cause of good immortality","rationale":"Retains ἀγαθῆς, which qualifies the immortality positively rather than asserting immortality without qualification."},{"source_quote":"τὴν τῶν πραγμάτων ζήτησιν καὶ εὕρεσιν","chosen":"the investigation and discovery of realities","rationale":"τὰ πράγματα denotes the matters or realities under philosophical investigation."},{"source_quote":"ἐταλάνιζον οὓς τὴν ἀρχὴν διὰ ἄγνοιαν μακαρίζειν ἐκινδύνευον","chosen":"I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of calling blessed","rationale":"Preserves the deliberate contrast between ταλανίζω and μακαρίζω."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.3","text":"From childhood, then, while absorbed in such lines of reasoning, I used to attend the philosophers’ schools in order to learn something certain. I found nothing except refutations and confirmations of doctrines, disputes and rivalries, techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises. At one time the claim would prevail—say, for example—that the soul is immortal, and at another that it is mortal. Whenever, then, an argument prevailed that it was immortal, I rejoiced; but whenever one prevailed that it was mortal, I grieved. Yet I was more disheartened because I could not establish either alternative securely in my own mind. Nevertheless, I perceived that opinions about the theses were judged false or true on account of their defenders and did not appear as they stood in relation to truth. Having at last realized, then, that comprehension does not arise from the theses being defended, but that opinions are pronounced on the basis of those defending them, and reeling still more amid these questions, I therefore groaned from the depth of my soul. For I was neither capable of establishing anything securely nor able to shake off concern about such things, although I wanted to, as I said earlier. For when I ordered myself, more and more frequently, to be still, somehow—I do not know how—the thought of such things would slip in upon me unnoticed and with pleasure.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς τὰς τῶν φιλοσόφων ἐφοίτων διατριβάς","chosen":"I used to attend the philosophers’ schools","rationale":"διατριβαί can denote lectures, discussions, or schools; “schools” conveys the recurring instructional setting."},{"source_quote":"δογμάτων ἀνασκευὰς καὶ κατασκευὰς","chosen":"refutations and confirmations of doctrines","rationale":"The paired rhetorical terms denote arguments against and arguments establishing or supporting positions."},{"source_quote":"λημμάτων ἐπινοίας","chosen":"inventions of premises","rationale":"In this logical context λήμματα are assumptions or premises used in argument."},{"source_quote":"αἱ δόξαι τῶν ὑποθέσεων παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας ψευδεῖς ἢ ἀληθεῖς ὑπολαμβάνονται","chosen":"opinions about the theses were judged false or true on account of their defenders","rationale":"ἐκδικεῖν here means to champion or defend a position, while παρά with the accusative identifies the defenders as the basis of the judgment."},{"source_quote":"οὐχ ὡς ἔχουσιν ἀληθείας φαίνονται","chosen":"did not appear as they stood in relation to truth","rationale":"The phrase is somewhat compressed; it can also be understood as “did not appear according to the truth they possessed.”"},{"source_quote":"ἐμαυτῷ πυκνότερον ἡσυχάζειν ἐπιτάσσοντος","chosen":"when I ordered myself, more and more frequently, to be still","rationale":"The first-person subject of the genitive participle is implicit but recoverable from ἐμαυτῷ and the surrounding narration."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐμαυτῷ πυκνότερον ἡσυχάζειν ἐπιτάσσοντος","issue":"The genitive participle has no expressed genitive subject. A first-person subject is readily supplied from ἐμαυτῷ and the context, though the construction may also be described as loose or anacoluthic. No emendation is required for a defensible translation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"1.4","text":"And again, at a loss, I would say to myself, “Why am I laboring for nothing? The matter is clear: if, once dead, I do not exist, it is not fitting for me to grieve while I now exist. So I will save grieving for that time, when, since I do not exist, I will not grieve. But if perhaps I do exist as something, grieving now is needless for me.” Immediately after this, another thought would enter me, for I would say, “Unless indeed I am destined to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now, if I have not lived devoutly, and, according to the accounts of some philosophers, I shall be handed over to Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus, like Sisyphus or Tityus or Ixion or Tantalus, and I will be in Hades, punished forever.” Again I would object in response, saying, “But these things are not real.” And again I would say, “But what if they are?” “Since the matter is uncertain, then,” I would say, “it is safer for me to live devoutly instead. And how will I be able, for the sake of what is right, while looking toward an uncertain hope, to master the body’s pleasures? But I am not even fully assured what exactly is right and pleasing to God; neither do I know whether the soul is immortal or mortal, nor is any certain argument to be found, nor can I rest from such thoughts.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τηρήσω τὸ λυπεῖσθαι εἰς τὴν τότε","chosen":"I will save grieving for that time","rationale":"The feminine article substantivizes an implied time or occasion; the paradox is that he will then be unable to grieve."},{"source_quote":"εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα εἰμί τι","chosen":"if perhaps I do exist as something","rationale":"Retains the indefinite τι and the possibility that some form of existence continues after death."},{"source_quote":"Εἰ μήτι γε τοῦ νῦν με λυποῦντος ἐκεῖ χεῖρον παθεῖν ἔχω","chosen":"Unless indeed I am destined to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now","rationale":"εἰ μήτι γε introduces an exception to the preceding claim; in context it could also be expressed rhetorically as “What if indeed...?”"},{"source_quote":"Πυριφλεγέθοντι καὶ Ταρτάρῳ","chosen":"to Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus","rationale":"The mythological names are transliterated without replacing them with generalized descriptions."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ᾅδου τὸν αἰῶνα κολαζόμενος","chosen":"in Hades, punished forever","rationale":"The accusative of duration τὸν αἰῶνα denotes punishment continuing through the age; “for the age” is a more formally literal alternative."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ δικαίου χάριν","chosen":"for the sake of what is right","rationale":"The substantivized adjective refers to right or just conduct rather than introducing a separate named doctrine of righteousness."},{"source_quote":"τί ποτε ἔστιν δίκαιον ἀρέσκον θεῷ πεπληροφόρημαι","chosen":"I am not even fully assured what exactly is right and pleasing to God","rationale":"πεπληροφόρημαι expresses settled or full assurance, and ἀρέσκον θεῷ qualifies what is right."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
